Confirmed — the file rename/history is continuous, and `a7d580522c762178aadcef72f72ba46a34a5b798` is the earliest commit introducing the unchecked `myDataChoices.size()` block; the later `fc2b7cc3b` is a pure whole-file reformat (every line touched) so blame attributes it there but the actual logic dates to `a7d58052`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: a7d580522c762178aadcef72f72ba46a34a5b798

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix in `b0c5379f` wraps an existing block (checking `myDataChoices.size() > 0 && myDataChoices.get(0) instanceof DerivedDataChoice`) with a new `if (myDataChoices != null)` guard. I ran `git log -p -S "usesTimeDriver"` on the file to trace when this exact block was first introduced, since a missing-null-check fix implies the code originally assumed non-null.

**(2) Culprit change:** Commit `a7d580522c762178aadcef72f72ba46a34a5b798` (Yuan Ho, 2011-11-02) added the block:
```java
if(myDataChoices.size() > 0 && myDataChoices.get(0) instanceof DerivedDataChoice){
    ...
}
```
directly after `if ( !init(myDataChoices)) { ... return; }`, with no null check on `myDataChoices` itself. This is the exact code that `b0c5379f` later wraps in `if (myDataChoices != null) { ... }`. All subsequent commits (including the large whitespace-only reformat `fc2b7cc3b` on 2012-08-13, which rewrote every line of the file and is why `git blame` on HEAD^ points there instead) only added formatting/logic elsewhere but preserved this unguarded access.

**(3) Evidence:** 
- `git show a7d580522c...` shows the block was newly added (`+` lines) with no surrounding null check.
- `fc2b7cc3b`'s diff for this file is a full-file rewrite (24422 changed lines out of ~12211 total, i.e., every line touched), confirming it's a mechanical reformat, not a logic change — it just re-attributes blame due to whitespace.
- Elsewhere in the same file (`DisplayControlImpl.java`), `myDataChoices` is explicitly checked for `null` before use in many other places (lines 2836, 2854, 2879, 3086, 3429, 3980, 5014, 5069), showing that null is an expected/reachable state for this field, and that the block added in `a7d580052c` was inconsistent with the file's established defensive-coding convention — supporting that this omission was the root cause of the NPE fixed in `b0c5379f`.

Confidence: high, based on direct historical trace of the exact vulnerable code fragment to its first introduction.
